useCase.title: Per-Provider Email Cadence and Content Personalization for HCPs
useCase.oneLiner: Learn each prescriber's preferred content, timing, frequency and format to cut email opt-outs.
useCase.personalizationTactic: Tailor send frequency, content, and timing per provider
cdpDataUsed: Email engagement history (opens, clicks, opt-outs) across brands
Preferred send time and channel signals
useCase.journey: The CDP unifies several years of email engagement data for healthcare providers across all brands, then a model scores each provider on preferred content, send times, frequency, and format. Brands are consolidated into one per-provider engagement plan. Providers who opened or clicked a topic receive more of it, while low-interest or over-contacted brands are throttled or suppressed. Plans refresh on a regular cadence, and the same preferences are shared with web and other channels so messaging stays consistent.
useCase.exampleBefore: A provider receives dozens of promotional emails a month from many brands, including ones unrelated to their practice, and opts out of all email.
useCase.exampleAfter: The provider gets two relevant emails a month on their preferred topic, sent on Tuesday mornings in a short format, and opt-outs fall by half.

kpis.primary: Email opt-out rate per provider segment

toolsNeeded: CDP with unified profile and identity resolution
Machine learning propensity and send-time model
Email service provider with frequency caps

useCase.title: Personalized Patient Website and Education Journey
useCase.oneLiner: Tailor patient website content, care prompts, and education by known condition and encounter data.
useCase.personalizationTactic: Show condition-specific content and care prompts based on encounters
useCase.journey: A patient visits the provider website or app. The CDP unifies known patient attributes (condition flags, recent encounter type, preferred location, declared interests) with anonymous browsing and search signals. Homepage and landing modules swap in relevant content: a find-a-PCP prompt for patients without a primary care provider, nearby specialists and closest open office hours, and education on the condition tied to a recent urgent care visit or search. The same segment drives matching follow-up emails with condition tips and appointment reminders, so the patient sees one consistent story across channels. Content must follow consent and health-privacy rules, so sensitive attributes are used only with explicit opt-in and never exposed in visible messaging.
useCase.exampleBefore: A patient who had a recent urgent care visit for a sinus infection lands on the homepage and sees the same generic service banners as every other visitor, then receives a generic newsletter a week later.
useCase.exampleAfter: The same patient sees a sinus-care guide, the closest open clinic with hours, and a book-appointment prompt on the homepage, followed by a matching email with self-care tips and a reminder for a follow-up visit.

kpis.primary: Appointment booking conversion rate from personalized web and email journeys
secondary: Patient portal and app engagement rate
Share of patients with a primary care provider linked
Email click-through rate on education content
Content engagement depth on condition pages

toolsNeeded: EHR or encounter data feed with consent management

useCase.title: Personalized Patient Appointment and Care-Reminder Emails
useCase.oneLiner: Tailor patient reminder and care-program emails by service line, preferences, and declared needs.
useCase.personalizationTactic: Vary reminder content and send timing by service line and preference
cdpDataUsed: Declared communication preferences and channel opt-ins
Web portal engagement and content views
useCase.journey: A patient books an appointment or enrolls in a care program on the provider's website. The CDP stores the service line, appointment date, and communication preferences. Before each visit, the patient receives a tailored reminder email with prep instructions relevant to that service, a clear reschedule link, and a preferred send time. Patients who opt for fewer messages receive only essential reminders. Preference updates made in the portal flow back to the CDP and change future sends.
useCase.exampleBefore: All patients receive the same generic reminder email, sent at 8 a.m. on the day before the visit, with no prep details and a single unsubscribe option for all messages.
useCase.exampleAfter: A patient booked for a physical therapy session gets a reminder with warm-up instructions, a reschedule link, and a text-or-email choice, sent at their preferred time. Patients who limit messages receive only essential reminders, and unsubscribe rates fall.
toolsNeeded: Practice management or EHR scheduling system

useCase.title: Personalized Preventive Care Reminder Emails for Patients
useCase.oneLiner: Send patients screening and appointment reminders tailored to age, history, and declared preferences.
useCase.personalizationTactic: Tailor screening reminders by age, history, and channel preference
cdpDataUsed: Patient profile (first name, age, sex, location)
Declared communication preferences and topic interests
useCase.journey: A patient joins the provider's email list and declares preferred topics and contact frequency in a preference center. The CDP unifies profile, appointment, and care-gap data. When a screening or follow-up becomes due, the CDP triggers a reminder email whose content, timing, and call-to-action match the patient's age, sex, due item, and preferred frequency. If a patient opens but does not book, a single follow-up is sent after a set delay. Patients who stop engaging move to a lower-frequency educational track instead of being unsubscribed. Booking events and unsubscribes flow back to the CDP to suppress and refine future sends.
useCase.exampleBefore: A generic monthly newsletter goes to the entire patient list with the same "Schedule your checkup" message, regardless of age or care status.
useCase.exampleAfter: A 52-year-old patient overdue for a colorectal screening receives a short email with her name, the screening details, and a one-click booking link, sent on her preferred weekday morning. Patients who ignore it get one follow-up, then a lower-frequency track.

kpis.primary: Screening or appointment booking rate from reminder emails
secondary: Share of due screenings completed within 90 days

toolsNeeded: Email service provider with dynamic content
